children: Initial settlement of the €14.40-per-share tender offer brings the Italian commercial vehicle maker under Tata Motors' control, with a fresh offer window for minority shareholders from November 2 to 6

Tata Motors has completed the initial settlement of its tender offer for Italian commercial vehicle manufacturer Iveco Group, acquiring an 89.42 per cent stake and bringing the company under its control. The acquisition was executed through Tata Motors’ indirect wholly owned subsidiary, TML CV Holdings B.V., according to a regulatory filing on Friday.
The transaction involved the acquisition of 238.16 million Iveco shares at €14.40 per share. Following the settlement, Iveco has become an indirect subsidiary of Tata Motors.

The development follows objections from some minority shareholders over the valuation of Iveco. Activist investor Petrus Advisers had questioned the offer price, arguing that it undervalued the company. In response, Tata Motors increased its offer from €14.10 to €14.40 per share earlier this month.

With approximately 10.58 per cent of Iveco’s common share capital, excluding treasury shares, still outside Tata Motors’ ownership, the company will reopen the tender offer for five trading days, from November 2 to November 6.
The settlement for shares tendered during this additional window is scheduled for November 13.

Tata Motors said further details of the post-offer process would be announced in due course. These could include a voluntary purchase procedure, a Dutch legal squeeze-out or a post-offer demerger and liquidation. The company has not announced any further revision to the offer price.
The completion of the initial settlement has also resulted in changes to Iveco’s board and corporate governance structure.

Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran has been appointed chairperson of Iveco as a non-executive director. Tata Motors Group Chief Financial Officer P B Balaji and Executive Director Girish Wagh have also joined the board as non-executive directors.
Olof Persson will continue as Iveco’s chief executive officer. The six-member board also includes independent directors Guenter Butschek and Charles Nichols.
Iveco said all outstanding special voting shares had been repurchased for no consideration, leaving no such shares outstanding following the takeover.
The company has also advanced the announcement of its third-quarter financial results to November 3 from the earlier scheduled date of November 5.
Iveco reported revenue of €13.43 billion in calendar year 2025. The company employs approximately 33,000 people and operates 16 industrial sites and 22 research and development centres.
Its business operations span trucks, buses, powertrains and vehicle financing.

The acquisition brings together Tata Motors’ commercial vehicle operations in India and emerging markets with Iveco’s established presence in Europe and other international markets. Tata Motors has said the two businesses have complementary product portfolios and limited geographical and industrial overlap.
